title: Austin City Funds: Police, Fire & Cost Saving Plans
summary:
*   Austin officials met for a special work session dedicated to the proposed 1989-90 city budget.
*   Discussions included projections for city revenue sources like property and sales tax, alongside recommendations for employee wages and benefits.
*   A new "Cost Savings Incentive Program" was introduced, aiming to encourage efficiency across city departments.
*   Key public safety departments, including Police and Fire, presented their specific budget requests for the upcoming fiscal year.

SPECIAL CALLED COUNCIL MEETING
FIRST FLOOR ASSEMBLY ROOM OF TOWN LAKE CENTER
721 BARTON SPRINGS ROAD
Council Chambers, 307 West Second Street, Austin, Texas Mayor Cooke called to order the
special called meeting of the Council, noting the absence of Councilmembers Carl-Mitchell
and Humphrey. The Mayor said the purpose of the meeting was to hold a work session on the
proposed 1989-90 budget.
City Manager Barnett discussed the general fund revenue projections for property tax,
sales tax, transfers, fees and charges. Elaine Hart, Director of Finance, illustrated by
use of charts many of the projections. A copy of the charts are on file in the City
Clerk's office.
Council recessed its meeting from 11:50 to 1:50 Ρ.Μ.
When the meeting resumed a presentation and discussion of wage and benefit recommendations
for fiscal year 1989-90 was held. The information referred to by the speakers is on file
in the City Clerk's office.
City Manager Barnett introduced a discussion of a Cost Savings Incentive Program for City
departments. The explanation sheet is on file in the City Clerk's office.
Presentations of specific departments then began with Libby Watson, Assistant City Manager
and Chief of Police Jim Everett explaining the budget for the Police Department.
Fire Chief Roberts was next, with discussion concerning the budget for the Fire
Department.
The Council adjourned its meeting at 4:50 Ρ.Μ.
